headline: Classified and SME budgets permanently migrated to platforms; local newsroom unit economics broken.

deltas.from: Q1 2026: ad impressions baseline, avg price per ad baseline
deltas.to: Q2 2026: $60.801B quarterly revenue, +14% impressions YoY, +12% average price per ad
deltas.change: +14% impressions, +12% price per ad (double-digit growth sustained)
deltas.reads: Meta continues to absorb the ad budgets (especially SME and local-business spend) that historically funded local newsrooms; no slowdown visible in platform consolidation of advertiser budgets.

deltas.from: Q4 2024 (implied): political advertising + baseline local ads
deltas.to: Q4 2025: $549M total ad revenue, with political dropping $233M YoY to only $21M; Q2 2026 $862M but politically inflated again
deltas.change: Q4 2025 YoY: -42% political ad cliff; structural non-political ad weakness visible beneath political cycles
deltas.reads: Largest local broadcaster shows fundamental weakness in non-political advertising; when political windfall disappears, underlying local-business ad demand remains depressed, confirming permanent migration.

deltas.metric: revenue from open-internet and SME/mid-market advertiser spend
deltas.reads: Ad-tech middleman serving smaller advertisers and publishers shows sharp contraction; SME digital-ad budgets under pressure as businesses migrate direct-to-platform (Google, Meta) or abandon small-local-business advertising entirely.

deltas.metric: full-year revenue (reported basis including legacy drag)
deltas.reads: Open-internet programmatic platform shows revenue decline on reported basis; while management attributes drag to legacy DSP wind-down, the underlying signal is flattish growth in an infrastructure layer that depends on publisher demand and advertiser budgets fragmenting healthily.

deltas.from: 2025 annual: YouTube exceeded $60B of annual revenue in ads and subscriptions combined; Search dominant in core
deltas.to: Q2 2026: Google consolidated revenue $119.8B (largest search+ads business globally)
deltas.change: Sustained 80%+ of U.S. digital ad spend captured; no saturation signal
deltas.reads: Google's dominance in search and YouTube means local-business classifieds (used to fund local papers) flow to Google Properties Maps/Local Services Ads, not to local newsrooms or traditional publishers.

deltas.metric: Pay-TV subscriber base (proxy for cord-cutting and legacy-media household decline)
deltas.to: Q2 2026: 6.391M Pay-TV subscribers (deconsolidated, but still showing 607K decline in 6 months)
deltas.reads: Household video base collapsing; as TV households erode, advertising insert-spend opportunities for linear broadcast inventory (including local news) decline with them, even before budget migration to digital.

momentum_note: The local-news collapse trend is accelerating. Meta and Google are capturing double-digit growth in advertiser budgets (impressions +14%, pricing +12%) that once funded local newsrooms through classifieds and SME spend. Nexstar's Q4 2025 advertising cliff and Q2 2026 political rebound mask structural weakness in non-political local advertising. Teads and PubMatic (the open-internet infrastructure layer) show contraction (-17% and -3% respectively), confirming that smaller advertisers either moved directly to platforms or reduced local advertising spend. Pay-TV subscriber decline (-8.7% annualized) further erodes the insert-ad and linear-broadcast base that underpinned local-news economics. No company in these filings shows a working unit-economics fix for local journalism when classified and SME budgets have permanently migrated to platforms.
